areas_of_law: Federal public service staffing and employment law
issues: What is the applicable standard for pre-hearing production/disclosure before the Canadian Human Rights Tribunal, and is a complainant entitled to a higher standard than the Tribunal's own rules based on the seriousness of the allegations?

Whether documents are 'arguably relevant' to the individual failure-to-accommodate claim and to the systemic discriminatory policy/practice claim, and how that test applies to internal emails, briefing notes and memos involving named managers
Whether records of accommodation provided to the complainant in other, unrelated staffing competitions are producible
Whether the psychology centre's assessment/analysis of the complainant's accommodation options is producible, and whether it is protected by privilege or medical confidentiality
Whether the applications, resumes and personal information of other unsuccessful candidates are producible given competing privacy interests
Whether documents relating to an unrelated harassment allegation against one manager are relevant to the discrimination complaint

Whether executive performance agreements tying managers' compensation to employment equity targets are relevant to a human rights complaint, and the relationship between employment equity legislation and human rights legislation

Whether the employer's 'right fit' selection standard, applied at the appointment-from-pool stage, constitutes a discriminatory policy or practice, and what the appropriate accommodation remedy is (direct appointment vs. re-assessment) where the complainant refused a proposed accommodation process
key_facts: Complainant is a federal government engineer with a disability-related medical condition
He applied for a senior engineering position without initially disclosing his condition; was assessed and placed in a qualified pool
He was told his interview was 'OK' and he would not be selected once the position was created
He then self-identified as disabled and requested accommodation, arguing direct appointment from the pool was the only meaningful accommodation
He alleges the department's 'right fit' selection standard is itself discriminatory against people with his condition (systemic claim) in addition to an individual failure to accommodate
Employer offered to have the psychology centre assess needed accommodations and re-run the assessment; complainant refused to attend
Complaint is before a human rights tribunal at the pre-hearing/production stage

Complainant seeks broad production: communications involving nine named managers over set periods; his accommodation records from three unrelated competitions; the full psychology centre analysis; other candidates' applications/resumes; harassment-related documents about one manager; executive performance agreements of two senior managers tied to employment equity targets
Employer objects that requests are irrelevant, a fishing expedition, and that employment equity legislation operates independently of human rights legislation
Complainant argues the seriousness of the case entitles him to a higher disclosure standard than the tribunal's rules provide
causes_of_action: Discrimination in employment on the basis of disability (failure to accommodate)
Discriminatory policy or practice claim (systemic discrimination)
candidate_statutes: Canadian Human Rights Tribunal Rules of Procedure
